Medical  Reading  Event  Category:  Health  Science
………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………
 
Eligible  Divisions:  Secondary  &  Postsecondary/  Collegiate  
Round  One:  50  Q  test  (60  minutes)  Digital  Upload:  NO  
Solo  Event:  1  competitor   
New  for  2026-2027
 Editorial  changes  have  been  made.   
Event  Summary
 Medical  Reading  allows  Secondary  and  Postsecondary/Collegiate  members  to  improve  their  reading  comprehension  and  
understanding
 
of
 
particular
 
topics
 
related
 
to
 
leadership
 
development
 
and
 
the
 
health
 
community.
 
This
 
competitive
 
event
 
shall
 
be
 
a
 
written
 
test
 
of
 
information
 
and
 
knowledge
 
gained
 
from
 
reading
 
the
 
selected
 
books
 
for
 
the
 
current
 
year.
 
Competitors
 
will
 
apply,
 
analyze,
 
synthesize,
 
and/or
 
evaluate
 
the
 
reading
 
material
 
in
 
a
 
multiple-choice
 
test.
 
This
 
event
 
aims
 
to
 
inspire
 
members
 
to
 
be
 
proactive
 
future
 
health
 
professionals
 
and
 
apply
 
the
 
knowledge
 
gained
 
from
 
reading
 
medical
 
and
 
leadership
 
books.
 
  
General  Event  Information
 
General  Rules   Competitors  must  be  familiar  with  and  adhere  to  the  General  Rules  and  Regulations.   Books  for  this  event  are  continually  recommended  by  membership,  vetted  through  the  HOSA  Medical  Reading  Committee  over  the  previous  school  year,  and  selected  each  June  by  the  HOSA  Competitive  Events  Leadership.   Books  chosen  for  this  event  are  believed  to  enhance  HOSA  members’  journey  in  this  division,  but  parents  and  advisors  are  encouraged  to  review  this  list  to  ensure  this  year’s  selections  are  the  best  ﬁt  for  your  student.  
Dress  Code  Proper  business  attire  or  ofﬁcial  HOSA  uniform.  Bonus  points  will  be  awarded  for  proper  dress.   
Competitors  Must  Provide  ●  Photo  ID ●  Two  #2  lead  pencils  (not  mechanical)  with  an  eraser  ●  Neon  colored  foam  earplugs,  NOT  earbuds,  for  noise  control  (optional)  HOSA  Conference  Staff  will  provide  equipment  and  supplies  listed  in  Appendix  I.  
Ofﬁcial  References   The  references  below  are  used  in  the  development  of  the  test  questions:  ●  Crisis  Averted;  The  Hidden  Science  of  Fighting  Outbreaks by  Caitlin  Rivers  ●  Everything  is  Tuberculosis:  The  History  and  Persistence  of  Our  Deadliest  Infection by  John  Green  ●  Fragmented:  A  Doctor's  Quest  to  Piece  Together  American  Healthcare by  Ilana  Yurkiewicz  MD  ●  The  Next  Patient:  The  Incredible  World  of  Emergency  Medicine by  Dr.  J.  Thomas  Grant  ●  Grit:   The  Power  of  Passion  and  Perseverance by  Angela  Duckworth  
      Medical  Reading   ILC  Guidelines  (September  2026)          Page  1  of  2  The  expectation  is  that  competitors  read  and  are  aware  of  all  the  content  within  these  guidelines  and  associated  links.  Successful  competitors  will  study  all  links  for  the  detailed  information.   

ROUND  ONE-  Test
 
Test  Instructions  All  competitors  will  be  given  a  test  and  test  answer  sheet.  The  written  test  consists  of  50  multiple-choice  questions  (10  questions  per  book)  in  a  maximum  of  60-minutes.  See  test  instructions  here.  An  essay  tiebreaker  question  will  be  administered  with  the  original  test.   Essay  tiebreakers  will  be  completed  on  the  back  of  the  test  answer  sheet.  
Time  Remaining  Announcements  
There  will  be  NO  verbal  announcements  for  time  remaining  during  ILC  testing.   All  ILC  testing  will  be  completed  in  the  Testing  Center,  and  competitors  are  responsible  for  monitoring  their  own  time.  
Sample  Test  Questions  (Samples  are  from  a  previous  year)  
Radium  Girls  1.  The  symptoms  of  radium  poisoning  are  very  similar  to  poisoning  from  which  other  chemical?  (pp  21)  A.    Bromine  B.    Carbon  C.    Lead  D.    Phosphorus  2.  What  was  the  nickname  given  to  the  girls  who  shined  at  night  from  the  radium  powder?  (pp  44)  A.  Ghost  girls  B.  Shimmering  girls  C.  Radiant  girls  D.  Lustrous  girls  3.  How  did  Mollie  Maggia  die?  (pp  39)  A.  Increased  blood  volume  due  to  increased  number  of  red  cells  B.  Hemorrhaging  from  the  jugular  vein  C.  Bone  necrosis  and  bone  cancer  D.  Breast  cancer  with  metastasis  to  the  brain   
Final  Scoring 
 In  the  event  of  a  tie,  the  essay  will  be  judged  to  break  the  tie.    
Future  Opportunities:   The  HOSA  Scholarship  program  has  funding  available  for  HOSA  members  who  have  an  interest  in  various  health  careers!   The  application  process  begins  January  1,  2027,  and  can  be  found  here: https://hosa.org/scholarships/.   Graduating  from  high  school  or  completing  your  postsecondary/collegiate  program  does  not  mean  your  HOSA  journey  has  to  
end.
